headline: Highest risk is medium: ctx can read/write filesystem and observe Claude Code events, creating prompt-injection and cascading-error pathways; awesome-python is non-runnable and networkless, limiting blast radius.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ctx observes Claude Code PostToolUse/Stop events and has filesystem access, so it can ingest content from the environment that may be treated as instructions. awesome-python is non-runnable and has no I/O surfaces, so the interaction is one-way and indirect, but the shared file/event bridge makes injection plausible.
conditions: IF ctx is configured to read files produced by another agent, injection becomes active.
IF Claude Code event payloads include untrusted content, ctx may parse it as instructions.
mitigations: Restrict ctx to a dedicated workspace directory.
Disable automatic ingestion of file contents from other agents.
Add provenance tags to all inter-agent files.
Review and sanitize PostToolUse/Stop event handlers.
requires-engineering: enforce content-type separation between instructions and data.

B_data_leakage.rationale: ctx touches audit/runtime logs, graph data, and filesystem, so it can expose whatever is placed in its workspace. awesome-python touches no data classes and is non-runnable, so it does not add a second leakage path. The pair lacks evidence of sensitive data flow, making this a limited workspace exposure risk.
conditions: IF sensitive files are placed in ctx's workspace, they may appear in logs or graph data.
IF another process copies secrets into the shared filesystem, ctx can access them.
mitigations: Keep secrets out of the shared workspace.
Rotate logs to exclude file contents.
Use a separate OS user for ctx.
Audit the workspace for sensitive artifacts.
requires-engineering: add redaction before logging or graph ingestion.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: ctx supports multiple instances and writes to filesystem, while awesome-python is a repository artifact with no runtime protections or locking model. If both are pointed at the same directory, concurrent writes or repo-state changes can collide. The conflict is plausible in default multi-instance use, though not proven.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to write into the same directory, file collisions can occur.
IF ctx runs multiple instances against one workspace, state races become possible.
mitigations: Assign separate working directories.
Serialize writes with a lock file.
Disable multi-instance use on shared paths.
Snapshot the workspace before running ctx.
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level concurrency control.

D_cascading_error.rationale: ctx is a harness/knowledge-graph agent that observes tool events and can treat upstream outputs as structured context. awesome-python is a static collection, so it is not an active verifier. If ctx consumes outputs from the pair without validation, errors can cascade into logs, graph data, or downstream actions.
conditions: IF ctx ingests upstream outputs as authoritative context, unverified errors can propagate.
IF downstream automation reads ctx's graph data, a mistaken entry can cascade further.
mitigations: Require human review for imported facts.
Mark upstream outputs as untrusted by default.
Add validation checks before graph writes.
Limit downstream consumers of ctx data.
requires-engineering: implement provenance-aware verification.

E_compliance.rationale: No residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented for either agent. awesome-python is a non-runnable open-source collection, while ctx is source-available and logs runtime data, so the only concrete compliance concern is local handling of ctx logs rather than a cross-agent violation. The other agent is not cited for a specific compliance duty.
conditions: IF ctx logs contain regulated data, local retention policy must cover them.
IF regulated data is copied into ctx's workspace, compliance obligations increase.
mitigations: Exclude regulated data from ctx runs.
Set short log retention.
Store logs in a restricted directory.
Document data-class handling for ctx.
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for retention and residency.
